title: Latency capture degeneracy lab notes — sprint 46 sync
body:
Meeting: Latency capture degeneracy lab — weekly sync
Date: 2026-11-18
Attendees: Maya (owner), Liam, Sofia, Noah, Priya, +1 (on-call)
Location: Zoom / #perf-bench-sync

Purpose
- Capture recent runs that showed non-linear tail growth (what we're calling `degeneracy`) in mixed-seq workloads.
- Triage hypotheses, decide follow-ups and short experiments for next 48 hours.

Quick summary / TL;DR
- Reproduced degeneracy spike in lab with version v0.9.12-rc (nightly build). Spike occurs after ~18–24 minutes of sustained mixed workload with 20% long sequences (>1024).
- KV-cache eviction patterns correlate with 97th+ percentile jumps; but not sufficient to explain 99.9th. Suspect interplay between batching heuristics + GC/allocator fragmentation on newer kernels.
- Short experiments planned: (A) fixed small-batch shadow runs w/ KV prewarm, (B) disable adaptive batching for 30m window, (C) isolate allocator variant (jemalloc vs tcmalloc) in synthetic harness.

Run log (most relevant runs)
- run-id: degen-lab-20261118-a (v0.9.12-rc, 8xA10g, mixed-seq, qps=450)
  - start 10:05, observed 97th latency = 63ms (baseline 28ms), 99.9th = 1.2s (baseline 180ms) at minute 21.
  - traces: trace://bf3a7c9e-61d4-4c8a-9f3b-2d7e5b1a9c11 (sampled 12 slow requests)
  - note: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 71% leading up to spike.

- run-id: degen-lab-20261118-b (v0.9.11-stable, same infra)
  - no degeneracy spike during 60m run. 97th stayed under 40ms.
  - suggests regressions introduced between 0.9.11 -> 0.9.12-rc (candidate commits: PR#4300, PR#4312).

Observations & early hypotheses
1) KV-cache eviction temperature: bursts of long sequences push long-lived KV entries out, leading to cache-miss storms when subsequent short requests need to reconstruct KV state. Hypothesis: prefix cache indexing/regeneration has corner-case O(N) behavior under churn.
2) Adaptive batching interaction: when a KV-miss occurs and request latency increases, adaptive batching heuristics attempt to reclaim throughput by expanding batch windows, but expanded batches collide with short-deadline requests causing amplified tail.
3) Allocator fragmentation / background GC: multiple teams reported more memory churn in 0.9.12-rc. Fragmentation can cause long pauses on allocation paths used during KV rebuild.
4) Kernel upgrade timing: observed runs on nodes with Linux 6.3 had slightly higher baseline tail (not the main factor but additive).

Evidence matrix (notes)
- KV-hit-rate correlation: strong with 97th (r≈0.82), weaker with 99.9th (r≈0.5) — implies KV misses necessary but not sufficient for extreme tails.
- PR#4312 (async-scheduler tweak) landed between versions and changes batching timeouts. Reverting locally removed some spikes in a micrograph run.
- jemalloc -> tcmalloc test reduced allocation-related pauses in a small reproduce harness (no KV churn) — points at allocator contribution.

Short experiments (48h horizon)
- A: KV prewarm + LRU hysteresis (shadow)
  - What: enable manual prewarm for first 10% of sequences and increase LRU hysteresis window by 2x.
  - Why: make KV churn less likely during the first 30 minutes after load increases.
  - Owner: Liam. Start: 2026-11-18 15:00 PST. Run length: 60m x 3.

- B: Adaptive batching off (control)
  - What: disable adaptive batching (force fixed batch window 4ms).
  - Why: if adaptive expansion amplifies tail, disabling should reduce 99.9th.
  - Owner: Sofia. Start: 2026-11-18 18:00 PST. Run length: 30m x 4.

- C: Allocator swap matrix
  - What: run synthetic run with jemalloc (baseline), tcmalloc, and system malloc variants on same image. Track minor/major pauses.
  - Why: isolate allocator pause contribution.
  - Owner: Noah. Start: 2026-11-19 09:00 PST. Run length: 45m each.

- D: Canary revert of PR#4312 in staging image
  - What: build image with PR#4312 reverted and run the mixed-seq schedule.
  - Owner: Priya. Blocking: need CI artifacts from release-engineering. ETA: 2026-11-19 EOD.

Metrics to collect (make sure run harness captures these)
- per-request KV-hit/miss + reason tag (prefix, prompt, seq-len).
- batch-size distribution over time + per-batch latency histogram.
- allocator internal stats (heap fragmentation, arenas) sampled every 10s.
- OS-level soft-irqs and scheduler load snapshot at 1s resolution for spike windows.
- full trace for all requests > 300ms (sample-limit 200 per run).

Open questions / unknowns
- Why does 99.9th sometimes appear with low KV miss-rate? (Possible: single long allocation or system pause). Need full stack trace for >1s requests.
- Are there cross-tenant batch fusion interactions in shared GPU pools that amplify spikes? (run isolation tests next sprint)
- Does the model runtime warming path (first few KV loads) block on synchronous IO in specific ops introduced by PR#4300?

Notes-to-self (informal)
- Check linked traces for slow-request callstacks around token-generation loop (look for repeated mutex contention logs).
- Add a synthetic workload that flips sequence length distribution mid-run to force cache churn (useful for stress test).
- Reminder: capture process pprof at minute 18 for all runs to get stack snapshots.

Decisions made in meeting
- Prioritize experiments A–C in parallel; revert PR#4312 only if C and B don't sufficiently mitigate.
- Keep production routing policy unchanged for now; add extra telemetry and a short-lived canary lane to test fixed-batch in prod traffic (controlled).

Action items (owner, due)
- Liam: provision KV prewarm shadow cluster + run A (due 2026-11-19 12:00 PST)
- Sofia: schedule adaptive-batching-off runs B and push results to /bench/results/degen-20261118 (due 2026-11-19 09:00 PST)
- Noah: run allocator matrix C and upload perf counters (due 2026-11-20 10:00 PST)
- Priya: attempt staging revert D, coordinate with release-eng (update by 2026-11-19 EOD)
- Maya: aggregate traces and prepare short summary for Product/Support if trend persists (due 2026-11-20)

Risks / rollback notes
- Reverting PR#4312 may reduce throughput under high sustained qps; only revert in canary if telemetry indicates net latency win.
- Disabling adaptive batching in prod will increase per-token cost; runs will quantify economic impact.

Follow-ups (next sync)
- Quick standup 2026-11-19 11:00 to check experiment health and early metrics.
- Full review 2026-11-20 with assembled traces and pprof dumps.

Appendix: quick timeline of related commits (high level)
- 2026-11-04: PR#4292 batching heuristics tweaks (minor)
- 2026-11-10: PR#4300 kv-cache indexing change (introduces new eviction path)
- 2026-11-14: PR#4312 async-scheduler changes (affects batching timeouts)

End notes
- This doc is intentionally informal — use as working running journal. Add experiment outputs (links) as they appear.
- If you copy results into Confluence, keep link to this doc as canonical lab notes.

-- Maya
